bugs.error_message: A newly saved alias was not available in the shell that launched the TUI.
bugs.root_cause: The TUI runs as a child process and cannot mutate the parent shell; the existing shell had not loaded the new profile wrapper.
bugs.fix: Install a profile-managed alias-manager function that sources the generated alias file after successful exit; reload the profile once in already-running shells.

bugs.error_message: OpenCode sessions keep 'New session - …' placeholder titles; log shows agent=title stream error: AI_APICallError: Bad Request (providerID=venice, modelID=z-ai-glm-5-3-flash).
bugs.root_cause: Venice rejects the title agent's request shape for z-ai-glm-5-3-flash (the small_model); the model works fine for main-agent calls, only the title-agent request fails.
bugs.fix: Set small_model to venice/deepseek-v4-flash in opencode.json. Verified: new sessions get generated titles. Existing placeholder sessions are never re-titled (title gen runs only on a new session's first exchange).

bugs.error_message: On macOS, the alias-manager TUI shows no 'system' aliases, unlike the user's Linux machine where distro-shipped .bashrc aliases appear.
bugs.root_cause: discover_aliases only text-scans the profile file and its literal source/. targets, and deliberately never executes that text. It therefore cannot see aliases a shell defines internally at interactive startup (confirmed via `zsh -f -i -c alias` still printing zsh's built-in `run-help=man` and `which-command=whence`, from no file at all) or anything set by conditional/plugin logic. The user's macOS ~/.zshrc genuinely has zero `alias` lines (only tool-managed blocks), so the static scanner correctly found nothing there; the Linux comparison only worked because that distro's .bashrc happens to contain literal alias text.
bugs.fix: Added discover_live_aliases(shell), which runs `shell -i -c alias` in a timeout-bounded (5s), killed-on-timeout child process and parses its real alias output (parse_alias_dump_line, handles both bash's `alias name='value'` and zsh's `name=value` formats via the existing shell_words quoting parser). Merged over the static scan via merge_discovered_aliases (live wins on name conflicts) at the real CLI entry point in main.rs; discover_aliases itself is untouched so its existing hermetic tests still pass unmodified. Verified end-to-end on this Mac: native cargo test (17 passed, incl. two tests that spawn real bash/zsh with an isolated HOME and assert on real alias output), cargo clippy -D warnings clean, release build installed to /opt/homebrew/bin/alias-manager, and a real pty run (via `script`) entered the TUI's alternate screen and exited cleanly on SIGTERM with no panic. Also fixed a pre-existing clippy needless_return in default_config_dir's macOS/Windows cfg branches, uncovered because this was the first time clippy ran with the macOS cfg active.
